analysis.title: Boeing Co. (BA): 3Q26 First Take: Progress in the quarter
key_insights: BA 3Q26 free cash flow of $464mn beat GS's $150mn estimate and consensus of $330mn. Management is expected to give more commentary on the free cash flow trajectory beyond 2026 on the call.
Revenue of $24.19bn was above FactSet consensus of $23.95bn and above GS's $23.66bn estimate.

BCA operating income of $(697)mn compared with GS's $(327)mn estimate. GS attributes the gap to a less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs tied to production rate adjustments, and elevated supply chain costs.
BDS margin of 3.0% (adjusting out a divestiture gain) compared with GS's 2.7% estimate, helped by operational stabilization. Reported BDS margin was 6.2%.

The company continues to progress toward stabilized 737 production of 47/month. The 737-7 received amended type certification from the FAA during the quarter, followed by 737-10 certification in October.
The 787 program remained stable at a build rate of 8/month. The 777X program advanced 777-9 certification flight testing and remains on track for first delivery in 2027.

Reported diluted EPS was $(0.15) vs GS's $0.21 estimate, and core EPS was $(0.34) vs GS's $0.05. Total operating profit of $354mn compared with GS's $577mn, with unallocated items and eliminations of $(610)mn vs $(445)mn estimated.

GS rates BA Buy with a 12-month price target of $253, down from $277 on 29-Jul-26. The target is based on a 3.0% free cash flow yield on 2027E free cash. Price was $188.31 at the 26 Oct 2026 close, implying 34.4% upside.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 FCF of $464mn beat GS's $150mn estimate and consensus of $330mn, with progress on 737 rate and certifications. BCA operating loss was wider than GS expected. The $253 target is based on a 3.0% FCF yield on 2027E free cash.
